text: The redundancy carve-out compared field_arguments TEXT. Byte-identical argument text does not prove equal evaluated values (SetRange(Code, FilterVal) with FilterVal reassigned in-loop) nor the effective filter at loop entry (SetRange(Amt,0); SetRange(Amt,1); FindSet()).
evidence: A6 DROPPED. In-loop SetRange/SetFilter/SetCurrentKey disqualify unconditionally -- a deliberate conservative choice, stated as such rather than as proof that every repeated filter changes the set.

text: Deleting ALLOWED_OTHER_OPS removes an existing safety boundary: all_allowed requires EVERY non-Modify op to be on the list, so Delete/Insert/Validate/Get disqualify today. A predicate returning None for unmentioned ops would newly ACCEPT them, ADDING false positives.
evidence: Verified at d5.rs:108-114. The allow-list STAYS as the eligibility gate; the new predicate is a VETO layered on top and can only remove findings. A9 pins the previously-rejected companions as regression tests.

text: Terminator vs body Next must be distinguished: two individually unit-step advances still skip rows (repeat ... R.Next(); until R.Next() = 0). No argument predicate catches it.
evidence: Verified: is_terminator_next exists at mod.rs:827-829 and is used by d1/d2/d1_graph. REUSED UNCHANGED (strengthening it would move d1/d2, which ask a different question). Rule: exactly one eligible advance, is_terminator_next true, loop_stack.last() == the candidate loop id. Measured as P7 -- d5 reports the body-Next shape today.

text: d60 does not inspect ops on the DRIVER var at all -- its guard is record_variable_name != var_lc, i.e. only OTHER vars. The design said replace the list in both, but d60 has no list to replace.
evidence: Verified at d60.rs:145-151. d60 gains a NEW body pass over driver-var ops applying the same veto, with its own DetectorStats skip counter so the suppression is countable (A13).

text: The shape-2 fixture does not semantically narrow the set: SetRange(Amt, R.Amt) runs BEFORE R.Amt := 1, so R.Amt is still 0 and the setter reapplies the existing filter. It covers the row-dependent syntax, not a traversal change.
evidence: Shape 2 becomes SetRange("Entry No.", R."Entry No.") with no entry-number filter before retrieval, which genuinely narrows to the current row. A SetFilter case is added. The original is KEPT as a distinct syntax-shape case.

text: The Next literal rule must be exact: Next(+1), Next(-1), Next(0), Next(Step) and any expression must all disqualify, and None (unavailable) must never be read as an empty argument list.
evidence: kind is "integer" with value = RAW text (ir_walk.rs:399-402), so +1/-1 lower to unary expressions and are rejected. Three states separated in the acceptance: Some([]) eligible, Some([integer "1"]) eligible, everything else including None not eligible. A4 and A11 pin them.

text: The claim that the fix MUST move the serialized L2 contract is overstated: run_trigger is serde-skipped and still forwarded to L3, so an internal channel is technically viable.
evidence: Corrected to a deliberate CHOICE with its reason: an arity-only channel cannot separate Next(1)/Next(2)/Next(N), so it would need literal classification anyway -- a second private copy of what L2 already represents. Round 2 re-raised (WORDING ONLY): Classification and the What-P5-means section still called the contract move necessary. Both rewritten in v3 to state it as a chosen route with the alternative named.

text: Argument fields are OMITTED when None and in_until_condition is serde-skipped entirely; a query returning null for a missing key is not evidence the dump serialized a null field.
evidence: Wording tightened; the substantive conclusion (Next carries no argument info) stands on FIELD_ARGS_OPS excluding Next at record_op.rs:39-54, which is a source fact rather than a dump artifact. Round 2 re-raised (WORDING ONLY): P5 still said ops carry fieldArgumentInfos: null. Rewritten -- the field is OMITTED when None (features.rs:237 skip_serializing_if), so it is an absent key, and the conclusion rests on FIELD_ARGS_OPS excluding Next.

text: The terminator rule does not establish EXHAUSTION. until (R.Next() = 0) or StopNow modifies only the first row, and until R.Next() <> 0 has wrong polarity -- both have exactly one unit-step advance in the candidate loop own until and pass every v2 rule.
evidence: MEASURED: both counterexamples added to the fixture (CompoundTerminator, WrongPolarityTerminator) and both are REPORTED by d5 today, so the hole is live. But the fix is not available at this layer: PLoop (features.rs:292-298) carries only id, loop_type and source_anchor, and no terminator EXPRESSION is carried anywhere -- the only signal is the per-op boolean in_until_condition, which cannot separate a simple terminator from a compound one because the operator was never kept. The check is therefore a SECOND L2 feature on top of the one this issue needs, answering a different question. Scoped out, the traversal rules restated as necessary-not-sufficient, and filed as a discovery with both measured counterexamples as the reproducer. ROUND 3 RULING (astra): legitimately out of scope for #21 -- it requires separate knowledge of the enclosing termination expression, which neither PLoop nor is_terminator_next provides; both counterexamples are PRE-EXISTING false positives that adding only vetoes does not newly admit; and the design expressly disclaims exhaustion. Retained as the discovery reproducers.

text: A9 cannot promise the previously-rejected-companion baseline for BOTH detectors: d60 has no allow-list, so same-driver Delete/Insert/Validate/Get are rejected by neither its gates nor the new veto.
evidence: Accepted. A9 is scoped to d5 only, and d60 gap recorded as pre-existing rather than introduced here. Cardinality moved to a loop-level helper (the per-op predicate cannot count), and A4 gains Next(+1) and an expression case.
